claim: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) contributes significantly to chemotherapy resistance in advanced breast cancer.
source: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) contributes significantly to chemotherapy resistance and remains a critical challenge in treating advanced breast cancer.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise of the study.

claim: The complexity of EMT, involving redundant pro-EMT signaling pathways and its paradox reversal process (MET), has hindered the development of effective treatments.
source: The complexity of EMT, involving redundant pro-EMT signaling pathways and its paradox reversal process, mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET), has hindered the development of effective treatments.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract as background for the study.

claim: The study utilized a Tri-PyMT EMT lineage-tracing model in mice to analyze EMT status of tumor cells.
source: In this study, we utilized a Tri-PyMT EMT lineage-tracing model in mice and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to comprehensively analyze the EMT status of tumor cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the experimental model used.

claim: The study used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to comprehensively analyze the EMT status of tumor cells.
source: In this study, we utilized a Tri-PyMT EMT lineage-tracing model in mice and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to comprehensively analyze the EMT status of tumor cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the methodology used.

claim: Ribosome biogenesis (RiBi) is elevated during the transitioning phases of both EMT and MET processes.
source: Our findings revealed elevated ribosome biogenesis (RiBi) during the transitioning phases of both EMT and MET processes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: RiBi and its subsequent nascent protein synthesis are mediated by ERK and mTOR signalings.
source: RiBi and its subsequent nascent protein synthesis mediated by ERK and mTOR signalings are essential for EMT/MET completion.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the study.

claim: RiBi and its subsequent nascent protein synthesis are essential for EMT/MET completion.
source: RiBi and its subsequent nascent protein synthesis mediated by ERK and mTOR signalings are essential for EMT/MET completion.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the abstract.

claim: Inhibiting excessive RiBi genetically impaired the EMT/MET capability of tumor cells.
source: Importantly, inhibiting excessive RiBi genetically or pharmacologically impaired the EMT/MET capability of tumor cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this experimental result.

claim: Inhibiting excessive RiBi pharmacologically impaired the EMT/MET capability of tumor cells.
source: Importantly, inhibiting excessive RiBi genetically or pharmacologically impaired the EMT/MET capability of tumor cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this experimental result.

claim: Combining RiBi inhibition with chemotherapy drugs synergistically reduced metastatic outgrowth of epithelial and mesenchymal tumor cells under chemotherapies.
source: Combining RiBi inhibition with chemotherapy drugs synergistically reduced metastatic outgrowth of epithelial and mesenchymal tumor cells under chemotherapies.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Targeting the RiBi pathway presents a promising strategy for treating patients with advanced breast cancer.
source: Our study suggests that targeting the RiBi pathway presents a promising strategy for treating patients with advanced breast cancer.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: Multiple growth factors (TGFβ, EGF, Wnts, etc), signaling pathways (Smad2/3, PI3K/Akt, ERK1/2, etc), EMT transcription factors (Snail, Twist, Zeb1/2, etc), and hundreds of downstream EMT related genes are involved in the EMT program.
source: Multiple growth factors (TGFβ, EGF, Wnts, etc), signaling pathways (Smad2/3, PI3K/Akt, ERK1/2, etc), EMT transcription factors (Snail, Twist, Zeb1/2, etc), and hundreds of downstream EMT related genes are involved in the EMT program (Nieto et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nieto et al., 2016.

claim: The complexity of EMT leads to a wide spectrum of EMT phenotypes coexisting at different stages of tumors.
source: Such complexity leads to a wide spectrum of EMT phenotypes coexisting at different stages of tumors (Williams et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Williams et al., 2019 and Yang et al., 2020.

claim: EMT-endowed features contribute to tumor heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance.
source: The EMT-endowed features contribute to tumor heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance, making EMT an attractive therapeutic target.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Current EMT-targeting strategies focus on blocking EMT stimuli, signaling transduction, or mesenchymal features.
source: Current EMT-targeting strategies focus on blocking EMT stimuli, signaling transduction, or mesenchymal features (Williams et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Williams et al., 2019 and Yang et al., 2020.

claim: Current EMT-targeting approaches may paradoxically promote the reversed process of EMT, MET, which also contributes to malignancy development.
source: However, these approaches may paradoxically promote the reversed process of EMT, MET, which also contributes to malignancy development (Gao et al., 2012; Pei et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2012 and Pei et al., 2019.

claim: The Tri-PyMT model was developed by combining MMTV-PyMT, Fsp1(S100a4)-Cre, and Rosa26-mTmG transgenic mice.
source: To investigate the EMT process in metastatic tumor progression, we previously developed an EMT lineage-tracing model (Tri-PyMT) by combining MMTV-PyMT, Fsp1(S100a4)-Cre, and Rosa26-mTmG transgenic mice (Fischer et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fischer et al., 2015.

claim: The Tri-PyMT model traces EMT via a permanent RFP-to-GFP fluorescence switch induced by mesenchymal-specific Cre expression.
source: This model traces EMT via a permanent RFP-to-GFP fluorescence switch induced by mesenchymal-specific Cre expression.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the Tri-PyMT model.

claim: The absence of EMT reporting in metastatic lesions in the Tri-PyMT model has sparked a lively debate about the proper definition of EMT status in tumor cells and the biological significance of EMT in tumor progression.
source: The absence of EMT reporting in metastatic lesions in this model has sparked a lively debate about the proper definition of EMT status in tumor cells and the biological significance of EMT in tumor progression (Williams et al., 2019; Brabletz et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Williams et al., 2019 and Brabletz et al., 2018.

claim: Rheenen's group posited that the Fsp1-Cre mediated EMT lineage tracing model might not accurately capture the majority of EMT events in comparison to an E cadherin-CFP model.
source: Rheenen's group also posited that the Fsp1-Cre mediated EMT lineage tracing model might not accurately capture the majority of EMT events in comparison to an E cadherin-CFP model (Bornes et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bornes et al., 2019.

claim: Using the refined EMTracer animal models, Li et al., 2020 discovered that N-cadherin + cells, rather than the Vimintin + cells, were predominantly enriched in lung metastases.
source: Notably, using the refined EMTracer animal models, Li et al., 2020 discovered that N-cadherin + cells, rather than the Vimintin + cells, were predominantly enriched in lung metastases.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: The fluorescent marker switch of the established Tri-PyMT cell line reliably reports changes in EMT phenotypes.
source: In particular, the fluorescent marker switch of the established Tri-PyMT cell line reliably reports changes in EMT phenotypes (Fischer et al., 2015; Lourenco et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fischer et al., 2015 and Lourenco et al., 2020.

claim: Post-EMT(GFP+), mesenchymal tumor cells consistently demonstrated robust chemoresistant features compared to their parental epithelial cells (pre-EMT RFP+).
source: Importantly, post-EMT(GFP+), mesenchymal tumor cells consistently demonstrated robust chemoresistant features compared to their parental epithelial cells (pre-EMT RFP+) (Fischer et al., 2015), inspiring us to further study chemoresistance using the Tri-PyMT model.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fischer et al., 2015.

claim: RFP + Tri PyMT cells persist in the epithelial state (RFP+) in vivo.
source: In contrast to their persistence in the epithelial state (RFP+) in vivo (Fischer et al., 2015; Lourenco et al., 2020), RFP + Tri PyMT cells actively transition to GFP + in vitro in a growth medium containing 10% FBS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fischer et al., 2015 and Lourenco et al., 2020.

claim: RFP + Tri PyMT cells actively transition to GFP + in vitro in a growth medium containing 10% FBS.
source: In contrast to their persistence in the epithelial state (RFP+) in vivo (Fischer et al., 2015; Lourenco et al., 2020), RFP + Tri PyMT cells actively transition to GFP + in vitro in a growth medium containing 10% FBS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The fluorescence switch from RFP to GFP in Tri-PyMT cells is irreversible.
source: As the fluorescent switch is irreversible, GFP + cells accumulate over generations until a balanced ratio of RFP+/GFP + is reached.
evidence: This describes a property of the Tri-PyMT model.

claim: A subpopulation of Tri-PyMT cells that are double positive for RFP and GFP constitute approximately 2–5% of total cells.
source: Interestingly, we observed a subpopulation of cells, which were double positive for RFP and GFP, constituting approximately 2–5% of total cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: RFP+/GFP+ (Doub+) cells represent tumor cells transitioning from an epithelial to a mesenchymal state.
source: We posited that these RFP+/GFP+ (Doub+) cells represent tumor cells transitioning from an epithelial to a mesenchymal state, since their fluorescent marker cassette has switched to GFP expression induced by Fsp1-Cre, while pre-existing RFP protein lingers due to its tardy degradation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed data.

claim: Doub+ cells expressed intermediate levels of both epithelial markers (Epcam and E-cadherin) and the mesenchymal marker (Vimentin).
source: Indeed, immunoblotting analyses confirmed the association of the double positive fluorescence and a hybrid EMT status. Doub+ cells expressed intermediate levels of both epithelial markers (Epcam and E-cadherin) and the mesenchymal marker (Vimentin) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Doub+ cells have higher percentages of S and G2/M phase cells compared to RFP + and GFP + subpopulations.
source: Further characterization of the Doub+ cells revealed higher percentages of S and G2/M phase cells in the Doub+ population compared to the RFP + and GFP + subpopulations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Bulk RNA sequencing analysis revealed that Doub+ cells expressed both epithelial and mesenchymal markers.
source: Consistently, analysis of traditional EMT marker genes revealed that Doub+ cells expressed both epithelial and mesenchymal markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The KEGG_Ribosome pathway was significantly enriched in the Trans_Up gene list of Doub+ cells.
source: Interestingly, a gene set over-representative assay showed that the KEGG_Ribosome pathway was significantly enriched in the Trans_Up gene list (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by gene set analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated two major clusters of Tri-PyMT cells: one predominantly expressed epithelial genes, while the other displayed overall mesenchymal phenotypes.
source: The t-SNE plot demonstrated two major clusters (Figure 1C): one predominantly expressed epithelial genes, while the other displayed overall mesenchymal phenotypes.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cell trajectory analysis identified five cell states related to EMT status.
source: We, therefore, performed cell trajectory analysis (Monocle 2) based on all EMT-related genes (EMTome Vasaikar et al., 2021). Five cell states related to EMT status were identified (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by trajectory analysis shown in Figure 1D and cites Vasaikar et al., 2021.

claim: Trans cells gained expression of mesenchymal markers such as Cdh2, Vim, Fn1, and Zeb2, while retaining expression of epithelial markers such as Krt7.
source: Differential gene expression analysis confirmed that Trans cells gained expression of mesenchymal markers such as Cdh2, Vim, Fn1, and Zeb2, while retaining expression of epithelial markers such as Krt7 (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Among the 49 overlapped gene sets that represented significantly upregulated pathways when comparing Trans vs. Epi and Trans vs. Mes, six pathways were related to the ribosome or rRNA processing.
source: Among the 49 overlapped gene sets that represented significantly upregulated pathways when comparing Trans vs. Epi and Trans vs. Mes (p<0.05), six pathways were related to the ribosome or rRNA processing (Figure 1I, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: GSEA using scRNAseq confirmed significant enrichment of RiBi genes in Trans cells compared to cells at Epi or Mes phase.
source: Consistently, GSEA using scRNAseq confirmed significant enrichment of RiBi genes in Trans cells compared to cells at Epi or Mes phase (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: A significant trend of RiBi activation was observed in the transitioning phase of EMT.
source: A significant trend of RiBi activation was observed in the transitioning phase of EMT (Figure 1K, Figure 1—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1K and Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: The RiBi activity is lowest in cells characterized with the latest EMT pseudotime, indicating that the elevation of RiBi activities is transient during EMT.
source: It is worth noting that the RiBi activity is lowest in cells characterized with the latest EMT pseudotime, indicating that the elevation of RiBi activities is transient during EMT (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is an interpretation of data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: RT-PCR analysis confirmed the higher expression of RiBi-related genes in Doub+ cells compared to RFP + and GFP + cells.
source: RT-PCR analysis also confirmed the higher expression of RiBi-related genes in Doub+ cells compared to RFP + and GFP + cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Approximately 50% of GFP+/Epcam- Tri-PyMT cells expressed EpCam 4 weeks post-injection into Scid mice via tail vein, indicating active MET.
source: We sorted GFP+/Epcam- Tri-PyMT cells via flow cytometry and injected them into Scid mice via tail vein. Approximately 50% of tumor cells expressed EpCam 4 weeks post-injection, indicating active MET (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: GFP + cells from lungs formed two main clusters in the t-SNE plot, exhibiting overall epithelial or mesenchymal phenotypes.
source: Similar to our observations with in vitro cultured Tri-PyMT cells, GFP + cells from lungs formed two main clusters in the t-SNE plot, exhibiting overall epithelial or mesenchymal phenotypes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Trajectory analysis identified nine cell states with different EMT statuses in GFP+ cells from lungs.
source: We performed trajectory analysis with EMTome genes and identified nine cell states with different EMT statuses (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by trajectory analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Tumor cells with epithelial phenotypes displayed elevated RiBi activity during MET.
source: Consistent with the analysis for EMT, we found that tumor cells with epithelial phenotypes displayed elevated RiBi activity (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), indicating its reactivation during the MET process.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A significant positive correlation was detected between RiBi gene upregulation and MET pseudotime.
source: A significant positive correlation was detected between RiBi gene upregulation and MET pseudotime (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Doub+ cells exhibited significantly higher levels of phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase (p-ERK) compared to either RFP+ or GFP+ cells in response to serum stimulation.
source: In response to serum stimulation, Doub+ cells exhibited significantly higher levels of phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase (p-ERK) and phosphorylated mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (p-mTORC1) compared to either RFP+ or GFP+ cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Doub+ cells exhibited significantly higher levels of phosphorylated mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (p-mTORC1) compared to either RFP+ or GFP+ cells in response to serum stimulation.
source: In response to serum stimulation, Doub+ cells exhibited significantly higher levels of phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase (p-ERK) and phosphorylated mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (p-mTORC1) compared to either RFP+ or GFP+ cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The phosphorylation of Rps6 is regulated by synergistic crosstalk between mTORC1 and ERK signaling.
source: The phosphorylation of Rps6, an essential ribosome protein of the 40 S subunit, is regulated by synergistic crosstalk between mTORC1 and ERK signaling (Roux et al., 2007; Biever et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Roux et al., 2007 and Biever et al., 2015.

claim: Doub+ cells exhibited a significantly higher level of p-Rps6.
source: We thus explored the status of p-Rps6 and observed a significantly higher level of p-Rps6 in Doub+ cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Doub+ cells possessed enlarged cell sizes compared to RFP+ or GFP+ cells.
source: Flow cytometry analysis showed that Doub+ cells possessed enlarged cell sizes compared to RFP+ or GFP+ cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Doub+ cells exhibited an increased rate of nascent protein synthesis.
source: Using the O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) incorporation assay, we found that Doub+ cells exhibited an increased rate of nascent protein synthesis (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by OPP incorporation assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Doub+ cells had significantly more nucleoli compared to cells in epithelial (RFP+) and mesenchymal (GFP+) states.
source: By immunostaining Fibrillarin, a nucleolar marker (Ochs et al., 1985), we found that the Doub+ cells had significantly more nucleoli compared to cells in epithelial (RFP+) and mesenchymal (GFP+) states (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3D and cites Ochs et al., 1985.

claim: Doub+ cells had significantly higher transcription activity than RFP + and GFP + cells.
source: Consistently, using the EU incorporation assay, we found significantly higher transcription activity in Doub+ cells than in RFP + and GFP + cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by EU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transcription of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is mediated by RNA polymerase I (Pol I) in eukaryotic cells.
source: The transcription of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is mediated by RNA polymerase I (Pol I) in eukaryotic cells (Moss and Stefanovsky, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Moss and Stefanovsky, 2002.

claim: BMH21 and CX5461 are specific Pol I inhibitors, which inhibit rRNA transcription and disrupt ribosome assembly.
source: Small molecules such as BMH21 and CX5461 are specific Pol I inhibitors, which inhibit rRNA transcription and disrupt ribosome assembly (Haddach et al., 2012; Wei et al., 2018), providing a specific RiBi targeting strategy.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Haddach et al., 2012 and Wei et al., 2018.

claim: In contrast to the vehicle-treated RFP+/Epcam + cells, which transitioned to GFP+ upon serum stimulation, most cells treated with either BMH21 or CX5461 stayed in the RFP+ state.
source: In contrast to the vehicle-treated RFP+/Epcam + cells, which transitioned to GFP+ upon serum stimulation, most cells treated with either BMH21 or CX5461 stayed in the RFP+ state (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment of BMH21 or CX5461 inhibited the transcription activity in cells.
source: Of note, the treatment of BMH21 or CX5461 indeed inhibited the transcription activity in cells as detected by EU incorporation assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by EU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Pol I inhibitors significantly blocked the expression of mesenchymal markers, including Vimentin and Snail, while preserving the expression of the epithelial marker (E-cadherin).
source: Indeed, these Pol I inhibitors significantly blocked the expression of mesenchymal markers, including Vimentin and Snail, while preserving the expression of the epithelial marker (E-cadherin) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: BMH21 significantly prevented the Epcam retrieval by GFP+/Epcam- Tri-PyMT cells, suggesting the impaired MET capability upon treatment.
source: BMH21 significantly prevented the Epcam retrieval by GFP+/Epcam- Tri-PyMT cells, suggesting the impaired MET capability upon treatment (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Depleting one r-protein usually causes decreases of other r-proteins in the same subunit, and ultimately compromises the overall ribosome assembly.
source: Depleting one r-protein usually causes decreases of other r-proteins in the same subunit, and ultimately compromises the overall ribosome assembly (Robledo et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Robledo et al., 2008.

claim: Effective knocking-down of Rps24 or Rps28 significantly reduced the number of nucleoli.
source: Effective knocking-down of Rps24 or Rps28 significantly reduced the number of nucleoli (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Knocking-down of Rps24 or Rps28 impeded EMT (RFP to GFP switch) and reduced MET (regain of Epcam).
source: Accompanying the downregulated RiBi activities were the impeded EMT (RFP to GFP switch) and the similarly reduced MET (regain of Epcam) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: Treatment with cyclophosphamide (CTX) resulted in more GFP + cells, consistent with previous findings that chemoresistant features against CTX were acquired through EMT.
source: In contrast, treatment with the chemotherapy drug, cyclophosphamide (CTX), resulted in more GFP + cells (Figure 5A), consistent with our previous findings that chemoresistant features against CTX were acquired through EMT (Fischer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A and cites Fischer et al., 2015.

claim: BMH21 and CTX exhibited optimal synergy.
source: Interestingly, BMH21 and CTX exhibited optimal synergy (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by synergy analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At concentrations of 100–200 nM, BMH21 showed significantly high synergy scores with CTX (δhigh = 8.45).
source: Particularly at concentrations of 100–200 nM, BMH21 showed significantly high synergy scores with CTX (δhigh = 8.45).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from synergy analysis.

claim: The synergic effect between BMH21 and chemotherapy drugs is not limited to CTX.
source: Importantly, the synergic effect between BMH21 and chemotherapy drugs is not limited to CTX. We performed the combination treatment of BMH21 with the most commonly used chemo drugs of breast cancer therapy, including 5FU, Cisplatin, Doxorubicin, Gemcitabine, and Paclitaxol. Trends toward synergies were also found with most of them, especially with lower concentrations of BMH21(100–200 nM) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by combination treatment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The combination treatment of BMH21 and CTX exhibited the highest restraint on the chemoresistant outgrowth of metastatic tumors compared to the vehicle, BMH21, or CTX mono-treatment groups.
source: Bioluminescent imaging (BLI) revealed that the combination treatment exhibited the highest restraint on the chemoresistant outgrowth of metastatic tumors compared to the vehicle, BMH21, or CTX mono-treatment groups (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Both RFP + and GFP + cells were significantly decreased in mice receiving the combination therapy of BMH21 and CTX.
source: Both RFP + and GFP + cells were significantly decreased in mice receiving the combination therapy of BMH21 and CTX (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Many GFP+ cells displayed epithelial markers, such as EpCam, indicating that a MET process was involved during the outgrowth of lung metastasis.
source: Notably, many GFP+ cells displayed epithelial markers, such as EpCam (Figure 6C), indicating that a MET process was involved during the outgrowth of lung metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: CTX treatment eliminated the majority of RFP+/epithelial metastases, while the GFP+/mesenchymal cells showed survival advantages under chemotherapy.
source: CTX treatment eliminated the majority of RFP+/epithelial metastases, while the GFP+/mesenchymal cells showed survival advantages under chemotherapy, resulting in a higher ratio of GFP: RFP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Most tumor cells under BMH21 treatment kept their EMT phenotypes as RFP+/Epcam+ or GFP+/Epcam-, indicating the impaired EMT/MET transitioning by RiBi inhibition.
source: Interestingly, most tumor cells under BMH21 treatment kept their EMT phenotypes as RFP+/Epcam+ or GFP+/Epcam- (Figure 6C), indicating the impaired EMT/MET transitioning by RiBi inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The combination of BMH21 and CTX eliminated most tumor cells including both RFP + and GFP + cells, and significantly inhibited the outgrowth of metastatic nodules under chemotherapy.
source: Importantly, the combination of BMH21 and CTX eliminated most tumor cells including both RFP + and GFP + cells, and significantly inhibited the outgrowth of metastatic nodules under chemotherapy (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: LM2 cells predominantly exhibited a mesenchymal phenotype in vitro and gained Ecad expression during the outgrowth of lung nodules in vivo, indicating the involvement of the MET process.
source: The LM2 cells predominantly exhibited a mesenchymal phenotype in vitro and gained Ecad expression during the outgrowth of lung nodules in vivo (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), indicating the involvement of the MET process.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the LM2 model, BMH21 synergized with CTX, leading to a significantly lower metastatic LM2 tumor burden than the mock or mono-treatment groups.
source: Consistent with the Tri-PyMT model, BMH21 synergized with CTX, leading to a significantly lower metastatic LM2 tumor burden than the mock or mono-treatment groups (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: A trend of relatively higher RiBi activity was detected in tumor cells with lower EMT pseudotime in primary tumor cells from two breast cancer patients.
source: To further investigate the potential association of RiBi activity with EMT status of tumor cells in human breast cancer, we analyzed scRNA-seq data of primary tumor cells from two breast cancer patients (GSE 198745). A trend of relatively higher RiBi activity was detected in tumor cells with lower EMT pseudotime (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: A pattern showing the highest RiBi activity in EMT/MET transitioning phase was detected in the sample of patient B.
source: Interestingly, a pattern showing the highest RiBi activity in EMT/MET transitioning phase was detected in the sample of patient B (Figure 6—figure supplement 3F), indicating the similar role of RiBi upregulation in EMT status of breast cancer patients.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3F.

claim: Analyses of the survival data showed a significantly worse prognosis in the RiBiHigh group compared to the RiBiLow group in TCGA PanCancer Atlas and METABRIC databases.
source: The analyses of the survival data showed a significantly worse prognosis in the RiBiHigh group compared to the RiBiLow group (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by survival analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Prakash et al. found that elevated rRNA synthesis/RiBi pathway was concomitant with cell cycle arrest induced by TGFβ, fueling the EMT program in breast tumor cells.
source: Prakash et al. found that elevated rRNA synthesis/RiBi pathway was concomitant with cell cycle arrest induced by TGFβ, fueling the EMT program in breast tumor cells (Prakash et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Prakash et al., 2019.

claim: Using the Tri-PyMT model, the EMT transitioning (Doub+) cells had higher percentages of cells in the S and G2/M phases compared to the RFP + and GFP + cells.
source: Using the Tri-PyMT model, we found that the EMT transitioning (Doub+) cells had higher percentages of cells in the S and G2/M phases compared to the RFP + and GFP + cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: Ebright et al. identified a subpopulation of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in which high RiBi activities persisted to maintain their high metastatic potentials.
source: A more recent study identified a subpopulation of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in which high RiBi activities persisted to maintain their high metastatic potentials (Ebright et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ebright et al., 2020.

claim: The RiBi activity was associated with epithelial phenotypes rather than mesenchymal ones in CTCs.
source: Interestingly, the RiBi activity was associated with epithelial phenotypes rather than mesenchymal ones in CTCs (Ebright et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ebright et al., 2020.

claim: EMT induction by TGFβ primarily suppressed ribosome gene expression and global translational activity.
source: Indeed, EMT induction by TGFβ primarily suppressed ribosome gene expression and global translational activity (Ebright et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ebright et al., 2020.

claim: The RiBi pathway was transiently elevated during the transitioning phases of EMT/MET program.
source: By employing our unique EMT-lineage-tracing model, we discovered that the RiBi pathway was transiently elevated during the transitioning phases of EMT/MET program.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study.

claim: The enhanced activation of the RiBi pathway diminished as tumor cells accomplished phenotype changes.
source: The enhanced activation of the RiBi pathway diminished as tumor cells accomplished phenotype changes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: A lower RiBi activity was observed in the mesenchymal tumor cells than in the epithelial ones.
source: In general, a lower RiBi activity was observed in the mesenchymal tumor cells than in the epithelial ones.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: Targeting the RiBi pathway by RNase Pol I inhibitor impaired the EMT/MET transitioning capability of tumor cells and significantly synergized with common chemotherapeutics.
source: Targeting the RiBi pathway by RNase Pol I inhibitor impaired the EMT/MET transitioning capability of tumor cells and significantly synergized with common chemotherapeutics.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study.

claim: Some commonly used chemotherapeutics (Cisplatin, 5FU, Doxorubicin, etc), although primarily targeting DNA duplications, may also affect the RiBi pathway by inhibiting rRNA processing.
source: Of note, some commonly used chemotherapeutics (Cisplatin, 5FU, Doxorubicin, etc), although primarily targeting DNA duplications, may also affect the RiBi pathway by inhibiting rRNA processing (Burger et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Burger et al., 2010.

claim: RiBi is a process that is dysregulated in most, if not all, cancers.
source: Moreover, RiBi is a process that is dysregulated in most, if not all, cancers.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Tri-PyMT cells were established from primary tumors of MMTV-PyMT/Fsp1-Cre/Rosa26-mTmG transgenic mice.
